text_blocks.snippet: To determine if you no longer have COVID-19, you should focus on symptom resolution and testing. According to the CDC, you can consider yourself recovered when you haven't had a fever for at least 24 hours without using fever-reducing medication, your other symptoms are improving, and it has been at least five days since your symptoms started. The FDA also recommends taking multiple antigen tests (two for symptomatic individuals, three for those asymptomatic) to rule out continued infection, especially if you have had symptoms.
